text:
The Penguins have lost four straight and eight of their last ten, and the conversation around them has moved from fixing the season to selling it. Rickard Rakell's no-trade list reportedly stopped a deal to Chicago, according to TSN; Erik Karlsson and Evgeni Malkin fill the rumor columns, and even Sidney Crosby is being linked to Montreal and Ottawa. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's first-quarter report card gave low marks to both Crosby and Karlsson.

Here's what our numbers add: this team is worse in the standings than on the ice. At 7-14-2 and 16 points, Pittsburgh has 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and a 52% share at 5v5. It has scored 10.4 fewer goals than its chances predict, and our race model has the Penguins 7.5 points short of what their play has earned. The power play is the clear weakness, creating 0.41 expected goals a game.

The goaltending hasn't bailed them out. Arturs Silovs is 0-5-0 over his last five starts with a .857 save rate. Sunday's 1-0 loss in Dallas, against 33 saves from Jake Oettinger, was the kind of night that sums it up. Crosby's line with Rakell and Tommy Novak still has 57% of the expected goals.

Our playoff odds sit at 7%. What to watch is in the front office as much as on the ice: who Kyle Dubas moves, and whether the finishing turns before he does.
headline: Penguins slide, and the trade talk gets loud
